Five people, including three children, died Sunday afternoon, November 8, 2026, after an SUV plunged off an Interstate 10 overpass in Seguin, Texas.

According to the Seguin Police Department, the crash happened around 1:30 p.m. near Interstate 10 and FM 725, close to the Love's Travel Stop. A black Chevrolet Tahoe was traveling eastbound on I-10 when, for reasons still under investigation, it left the roadway, went off the overpass and crashed onto FM 725 below.

All five people in the vehicle — two adults and three children — died in the crash.

The identities and ages of the victims have not been released, pending notification of their families. Investigators have not determined what caused the SUV to leave the interstate.

Seguin police closed roads in both directions near FM 725 and I-10 while emergency crews responded and investigators examined the scene. Drivers were urged to avoid the area and use alternate routes.

This is a developing story, and Webb Watch 956 will update it as officials confirm more details.

Update — November 9, 2026

Seguin officials confirmed Monday that all five victims were from Harris County, in the Houston area, according to ABC13. Their identities and ages still have not been released, pending notification of their families, and officials have not said whether the victims were related. The Seguin Police Department is investigating the cause of the crash, examining the vehicle's condition, the driver's medical status and roadway conditions, according to reports.

Update — November 9, 2026 (afternoon)

Authorities have now identified the two adults killed in the crash as Omar Lumbreras Oliva, 30, and Ana Deli Lumbreras, 31, both of Porter, Texas, according to FOX 26 Houston. The three children were a 13-year-old boy, a 6-year-old girl and a 3-year-old girl; their names have not been released.

The crash happened about 12:56 p.m. Sunday, when the black Chevrolet Tahoe was traveling eastbound on I-10, left the roadway and fell from the overpass onto FM 725 below, according to reports. It was raining and the roadway was wet at the time. Guadalupe County Justice of the Peace Darrell Hunter said preliminary information suggested the vehicle may have hydroplaned, but the exact cause remains under investigation by the Seguin Police Department.

FM 725 reopened shortly after 6 p.m. Sunday, after a closure of about five hours.

Sources: Seguin Police Department; Angelo News; ABC13, November 9, 2026; FOX 26 Houston, November 9, 2026.

title: Five Dead, Including Three Children, After SUV Plunges Off I-10 Overpass in Seguin
